messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed steady memory growth on long-context workloads (>64k tokens) even after our existing compaction runs. frag_ratio jumping to ~0.42 after a few hours.

aj: Can you paste the profiler output? is it internal fragmentation (slab waste) or external (free holes)?

maria: Mostly internal. allocator reports many partially used blocks in the 256B and 1KB buckets. sample: `avg_block_used=0.37`, `bucket(256)=82k total / 54k used` — lots of small unused tails.

sandeep: Ran the trace harness last night with kv-prof — here's the trimmed output (5m run on canary):
```
kv-prof --trace=heaplets --duration=5m --out=trace.pb
SUMMARY: total_pages=12.1GB, used=7.3GB, free_gaps=1.9GB, frag_ratio=0.39
HOT: bucket-256: alloc_rate=14k/s, reclaim_rate=2.1k/s, avg_live_size=94B
HOT: bucket-1k: alloc_rate=4k/s, avg_live_size=420B
TRACE: frequent small tail frees at epoch boundaries, compaction skipped due to low contiguous runs
```

maria: thanks. looks like allocator fit policy (first-fit in slab) is leaving micro-holes that our compactor doesn't catch because contiguous-run requirement is too strict.

aj: Proposed idea: add a lightweight sampling collector that tracks fragmentation hotspots and triggers "micro-compacts" that are bucket-local, avoiding global defrag pauses. Micro-compact would merge adjacent free micro-blocks within a slab and relocate small live objects if beneficial.

elaine: Concern: relocation implies copying overhead and kv cache is hot in the serving path. micro-compactor must be low priority and non-blocking. Also need to ensure KV cache pinning (in-flight requests) won't see moved data.

aj: Agreed. Plan: 1) background compactor thread with yield points 2) versioned pointers + atomic swap for moved entries 3) sampling threshold set so we only act when free_fraction_in_slab > 0.25 and fragmented_runs > 128.

sandeep: I prototyped a versioned-pointer approach. Overhead is ~1.8% CPU at 50k qps in our sim, pause < 250us in worst-case when moving a 4KB set. I can share perf numbers.

perf-bot: Canary run 2024-02-03T08:12: perf delta — tail latency p95 +2ms, p99 +12ms during compaction windows (rare), average memory usage down ~7% over baseline after 3h.

maria: promising. we should also experiment with different block-size mixes. current bucket sizes are [64, 256, 1024, 4096]. What about introducing a 512B bucket to reduce internal fragmentation for medium tails?

aj: 512B might help; downside is extra metadata per bucket and more slab classes. Could support dynamic bucket split where we split 1KB -> 512B when we detect heavy 300-700B live distribution.

elaine: Also check how kernel selection and batching interact — larger batch sizes increase average token context lengths in-flight which could increase KV usage and change live-size distribution. We need cross-tests with batching heuristics.

maria: action plan I propose:
- A: run A/B canary with micro-compactor on 3 nodes (low traffic) for 48h (sandeep + infra)
- B: telemetry: add per-slab free-run histogram and live-size distribution metric (aj)
- C: bucket experiment: dynamic 1KB->512B split in sim (maria)
- D: batching matrix test (elaine + perf) to see interplay

aj: I'll open a PR for the micro-compactor sketch and the versioned-pointer ABI. keep it feature-flagged.

infra-bot: scheduled canary: kv-micro-compact-01 -> eng-runtime-canary at 1709460400 (3 nodes, 2h ramp).

maria: thanks. let's avoid any global stop-the-world compaction in this rollout. incremental only. if anyone sees p99 spikes above 50ms during canary, ping #eng-oncall immediately.

elaine: also add guardrail to never move entries pinned by active requests (check refcount>0).

sandeep: I'll post the sim perf matrix tomorrow with different bucket mixes. early note: 512B split reduced avg waste from 26%->18% in the sim for long-context traces.

maria: perfect. leaving notes for follow-ups in the PR. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Reminder: collect heaplet samples every 30m during canary and upload to /mnt/perf/canaries/1709456789/

maria: cool — follow-up sync next week after 48h run. thanks all.
